title: Tesla Renames FSD to ‘Tesla Assisted Driving’ in Europe
key_facts: Tesla renamed Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to 'Tesla Assisted Driving' in Europe; its European websites show the new name, as reported by Sawyer Merritt on X.
The change follows talks with Germany's Federal Ministry for Transport; Merritt says it should help with EU-wide approval.
Germany reportedly would back FSD in the EU vote if Tesla used the new name and capped speed at no more than 10% over the posted limit; Tesla has not confirmed the cap.
FSD's Speed Offset can currently exceed limits by up to 50% in some conditions; Sweden, France and road safety groups have raised speeding concerns.
The EU vote was delayed from 6 Oct to December at the earliest; Tesla needs a qualified majority of at least 15 countries.
Eight countries have already approved it; Germany has not yet approved it for its own roads.
quote_evidence: Tesla has officially renamed it “Tesla Assisted Driving” across the continent, and its European websites now show the new name, as reported by @SawyerMerritt on X.
Germany also wants Tesla to limit the system to exceeding the posted speed limit by no more than 10%.
The EU vote on bloc-wide approval was previously delayed from October 6 to December at the earliest.
why_it_matters_hint: The name change is a concession aimed at winning German and EU backing.
notes: Relies on an X post and reported ministry talks; Tesla has not confirmed the speed cap. Related to C11-02.
